title: Study in Italy
tagline: Public universities with English-taught programs and regional DSU scholarships.
intro:
Italy attracts students with affordable public universities, many English-taught programs and regional scholarships based on family income.

We shortlist programs, manage applications, and help with pre-enrollment, the scholarship and the national D visa.
services: Translation and legalization of documents, diploma evaluation
Advice on housing and first steps after arrival

sections.heading: How admission works
sections.body:
Admission usually has several stages: the university application, pre-enrollment via the national portal, recognition of your education documents and the visa. Some programs (such as medicine) have entrance tests.

Deadlines vary by university — many open applications as early as winter and spring.

sections.heading: DSU scholarships
sections.body: Regional **DSU** scholarships are awarded based on family income and can cover housing and meals and waive tuition. The application requires translated and legalized documents on family income and assets. We help you prepare this package.

documents: Family income documents — for the DSU scholarship
Proof of funds and accommodation — for the visa

steps.text: We apply for DSU and obtain the D visa.

faq.a: Not for English-taught programs — IELTS or TOEFL is enough. Basic Italian does make daily life much easier.

faq.q: Can I study in Italy for free?
faq.a: With a DSU scholarship many students are exempt from tuition and receive living support. Eligibility depends on family income.
Ideally 8–12 months before classes start: many universities open admissions early and paperwork takes time.
